assessments.reasoning: The Creative Commons capture at https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/1.0/legalcode spans 34,823 contiguous bytes. Its title, main h1, CC BY-NC 1.0 label and inline heading agree on variant and edition. The capture digest matches the claim revision.

The Index's pinned SCOPE.md admission row, bytes [533,639), requires controlling evidence of identifiable license text and edition. Creative Commons supplies both. The rule includes historical material and imposes no separate test of legal effectiveness for identifying a text.

The Index decision at bb181812e5fe13143c236554068f21d7ce34dd1e, bytes [1319,1538), lists b9e96b78016d4a9b95776cb3e7cc848c, CC-BY-NC-1.0, Attribution-NonCommercial 1.0 Generic, cc-by-nc-1-0-generic, sha256:706771a9a2ce7712c3474edc429ade20c7c94c74d48d04d696c524e03527f220, license, active. Each field matches the scoped mapping.

The BY-NC page's opening fine print refers to distribution of “THIS DRAFT LICENSE” while disclaiming an attorney-client relationship. Its significance for finality remains unresolved. That limitation is compatible with identifying the named text and edition.

challenge.method: Compared BY-NC with plain BY, the NoDerivs-NonCommercial variant, and the linked 4.0 International edition. Checked the heading, §§3–4, edition, capture and Index row separately from the draft notice.
challenge.results: The inspected text includes both “to create and reproduce Derivative Works” and the §4 commercial-advantage restriction. The adjacent variants differ on those passages. The page labels the linked 4.0 edition separately. Its own title and grant text identify the historical document without resolving finality.

limitations: Active denotes Index maintenance. The draft notice leaves finality and legal effect unresolved. Publisher currency, SPDX deprecation and release are outside that classification.

The live HTML digest is an acquisition observation. Equality with the declared /legalcode.en canonical representation, semantic equivalence, translations, project-file coverage, downstream grants and redistribution rights remain unverified.
